transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came because… well, because I don’t think I can keep this inside anymore. I keep telling my family, and some of the people at church, that it’s my fault my friend died. I didn’t call her back when I should have. She called, and I didn’t return it, and I keep going over it and over it in my head like if I had just picked up the phone, or called sooner, maybe things would be different.

And it isn’t just that. I had ugly thoughts sometimes—not that I wanted anything bad exactly, but thoughts I’m ashamed of—and now I know the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me. I can feel it, like it’s connected to what I did and what I thought. People tell me not to say that, but they don’t understand. It feels like I brought something terrible down on them. I’m the reason.
Do you find yourself thinking about these guilty feelings and thoughts over and over, even when you don’t want to?

Yes… yes, all the time. It just goes around and around, and I can’t make it stop even when I try to pray or distract myself. I keep telling them—my family, people at church—that I’m the reason my friend died, because she called and I didn’t call her back. And then I had those ugly thoughts sometimes, the kind I’m ashamed to even say out loud, and now it feels clear to me that the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me.

People keep saying, “That’s not true,” but they don’t understand how it sits in my mind. It’s there when I wake up, it’s there when I’m doing ordinary things, and I start thinking, if I had just answered, if I had just been a better person, if I hadn’t had those thoughts… maybe none of this would have happened. I know I sound like I’m repeating myself, but I can’t get away from it.
Do these thoughts about your friend and the guilt keep coming into your mind even when you don’t want them to, like they’re intrusive or uncontrollable?

Yes… yes, that’s exactly how it is. I don’t invite it in, I really don’t. I can be standing at the register, or washing a cup, or just trying to sit quietly, and suddenly there it is again—her calling me, me not calling back, and then this terrible certainty that I failed her.

I keep telling my family, and I keep telling people at church, even though I know they’re tired of hearing it, that I’m the reason my friend died. Because if I had called her back… if I had been the kind of person I should’ve been… maybe she would still be here. And then I think about those ugly thoughts I had sometimes, thoughts I’m ashamed of, and it feels like the Lord knows, of course He knows, and now everybody at church is being punished because of me.

I try not to think it. I try to push it away, but it comes right back, like it’s waiting for me. It feels uncontrollable. It feels true.

Do you find yourself doing anything over and over—like praying, asking for forgiveness, or performing certain actions—to try to make up for those thoughts or to stop feeling guilty or stop the punishment you think is happening?

I… I don’t know if I’d call it “doing something” exactly. I mean, I do pray, but I’ve always prayed, so it’s hard for me to tell what’s normal and what’s because of all this. Sometimes I ask God to forgive me, but I don’t have, like, a special thing I do a certain number of times or a routine like that.

Mostly it’s in my head. I go back over it and over it, and I say I’m sorry, but I don’t know that it makes anything stop. It doesn’t really feel like I can fix it by doing something. I wish I could. If there were a thing I could do to make it right, I think I would do it, but I don’t know what that would even be.
Do you ever feel driven to do certain things a specific number of times, or in a certain way, to try to prevent something bad from happening or to ease the guilt you’re feeling?

No… I don’t think so. Not like counting or having to do something three times, or touching things a certain way, if that’s what you mean. I don’t have a set way I do it, like if I don’t do this exact thing then something will happen.

I mean, I get stuck in it in my mind, terribly stuck, and I may pray or say I’m sorry to God, but it’s not organized like that. It’s not like I think, “If I say this prayer seven times, then it will stop,” or anything. I just feel guilty, and I keep turning it over and over, but I haven’t noticed myself doing some particular action a certain number of times to make it go away.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like going to church or spending time with family?

Yes… yes, I have. It’s like everything that used to make up my week just sort of fell away, and I don’t even have the strength to care about it.

I used to love choir. I really did. I liked standing there with everyone, knowing the hymns, feeling like I had a place. And the knitting circle too—those ladies would talk and laugh, and I’d work on my little projects, and it felt good to be around people. Bingo was something I looked forward to, even if it was just silly fun. And I used to like walking through Patterson Park, just to get some air and see the trees and the paths.

But now… now I mostly just sit in my chair. I sit there and think I should get up, I should get dressed, I should go, but none of it feels worth it. Even putting on clothes and getting myself together feels like too much for something that I know won’t feel good anyway. It’s not that those things changed. I changed, I guess. They just don’t reach me anymore.

Do you ever feel that your thoughts about being responsible for your friend’s death and the punishment on others are something more than just a worry — like they’re a truth you just know, even if others don’t see it that way?

Yes… I mean, that’s the hard part to explain, because people say, “Maybe you’re just worried,” or “Maybe you’re feeling guilty,” but it doesn’t feel like just a worry to me. It feels like something I know, deep down, even when everybody else acts like they don’t see it.

At church, especially… when the pastor says certain prayers, I hear it like he’s talking about me. Not saying my name, no, but the words line up in a way that feels… directed. Like God is warning me through him. And when the choir sings certain lines, the ones about sin or mercy or judgment, I just know they’re meant for me. I sit there and my stomach drops, because it feels like everyone may not understand it, but the message is there.

It’s like God has marked me. And the church is suffering because I brought this on us. I know that sounds strange when I say it out loud, and I know other people might say, “That’s not what the prayer meant,” but when I’m sitting there, hearing it, it’s not a maybe. It feels true. Like I’m being shown what I’ve done.
Do you believe that you are being punished for sins or wrongdoings in a way that you know is true, even though others might say that belief isn’t based in reality?

Yes… yes, I do. I know people keep telling me it isn’t like that, that I’m putting too much on myself, but it doesn’t feel like a thought I can just set down. It feels true.

I keep telling them I’m the reason my friend died. If I had called her back… if I hadn’t ignored that call, or waited, or whatever I did, she might still be here. And it wasn’t just that one thing. I had ugly thoughts sometimes too—impatient thoughts, selfish thoughts, thoughts I’m ashamed of—and I think the Lord saw all of that. I think He knew what was in me.

And now it feels like He’s punishing not just me, but everybody at church because of me. That’s the part that makes me feel so sick, because those people don’t deserve it. They’re good people. They pray, they sing, they do what they’re supposed to do. But I brought something bad onto them. I know others say, “No, that’s not real, that’s not how God works,” but I can’t believe them. I feel like I know it. I know I’m the reason.
Do you believe that God is directly communicating to you, or has marked you in some way, that your guilt has caused punishment on others?

Yes… yes, that’s what it feels like. I don’t know how to make it sound sensible to someone else, but when I’m in church and the pastor is praying, certain words just… they land on me. Like they aren’t just general prayers for everybody. They feel like they’re meant for me, like God is using him to tell me I’ve been marked.

And the choir too. I used to just hear the hymns as comfort, you know, something familiar. But now when they sing certain lines—about sin, or judgment, or needing mercy—it feels like a warning. Like I’m being told, right there in front of everyone, that this is because of me. That the church is suffering because I brought it on us.

People may say it’s just me taking things too personally, but sitting there, I know. I feel it so strongly. Like God is pointing it out to me, even if nobody else understands what’s happening.

Do you believe, without any doubt, that your guilt for not calling your friend back and having those thoughts has caused real, supernatural punishment on your church, in a way that you know is absolutely true, even if there’s no proof others can see?

Yes… I do. I know how it sounds when you say “no proof,” and I know other people would say there isn’t anything anyone can point to. But when I’m sitting there in church, it doesn’t feel like a guess or just me being upset.

When the pastor says the prayers, certain words feel like they are coming right at me. Not in a normal way, not just like a sermon that applies to everyone. It feels like God is using those prayers to warn me that I’ve been marked. And when the choir sings certain lines, especially about sin or mercy or judgment, I feel it in my whole body. I know they are really warning me.

It’s like the message is hidden from everyone else, or maybe they just don’t understand it, but I do. I hear it and I know the church is suffering because I brought this on us. I know people want me to say maybe I’m just feeling guilty, but it doesn’t feel like maybe. It feels absolutely true to me.
Do you ever feel that your guilt or sins are so great that they can never be forgiven, or that you are uniquely marked by God in a way that others cannot understand or see?

Yes… I do feel that. I feel like what I did can’t really be forgiven, not in the way people at church talk about forgiveness. They say the Lord forgives if you repent, and I’ve tried to repent, I have, over and over, but it doesn’t feel like it reaches Him. It feels like my prayers just stop somewhere because what I did was too bad.

I keep going back to my friend. I keep telling them—I keep telling everybody who will listen—that I’m the reason she died. If I had called her back when I should have, if I hadn’t been selfish or tired or irritated or whatever was wrong with me that day… maybe she would still be here. And it’s not only the phone call. It’s what was in my heart. I had ugly thoughts sometimes. Thoughts I shouldn’t have had. Mean, impatient thoughts. And I think the Lord saw all of that, not just what I did but what kind of person I really am inside.

And yes, I feel marked. I don’t think other people can see it the way I do, and they tell me I’m wrong, but I feel like God knows. I feel like He has singled me out because I brought this punishment on everybody at church. Those people don’t deserve to suffer because of me, but I know the Lord is punishing them because of what I did. That’s what makes it worse. If it were only me, maybe I could bear it, but I think I’ve brought it onto them too.
Do you believe that your thoughts or sins have caused supernatural consequences that others are unaware of, such as divine punishment that only you can perceive?

Yes… yes, I do believe that. I know other people don’t hear it the way I do, and I know if you were sitting beside me you might say it’s just a prayer or just a hymn, but it isn’t just that to me.

When the pastor is praying, certain words stand out like they’re being sent straight through him to me. It feels like God is warning me, like He has marked me because of what I’ve done. And when the choir sings certain lines—about sin, mercy, judgment, suffering—I can’t just hear them as songs anymore. I hear them as a message. A warning.

And I know others don’t seem to notice. They just sit there, they sing along, they bow their heads, they act like church is normal. But I feel it so strongly that the church is suffering because I brought this on us. Like the punishment is there, but only I understand why it’s happening. It’s because of me.

doctor.question: Do you believe, without any doubt, that your guilt for not calling your friend back and having those thoughts has caused real, supernatural punishment on your church, in a way that you know is absolutely true, even if there’s no proof others can see?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: When the pastor says the prayers or the choir sings certain lines, I know they are really warning me that God has marked me and that the church is suffering because I brought this on us.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly asking about a fixed, certain belief that guilt has caused supernatural punishment despite lack of proof or others disagreeing.

patient.answer:
Yes… I do. I know how it sounds when you say “no proof,” and I know other people would say there isn’t anything anyone can point to. But when I’m sitting there in church, it doesn’t feel like a guess or just me being upset.

When the pastor says the prayers, certain words feel like they are coming right at me. Not in a normal way, not just like a sermon that applies to everyone. It feels like God is using those prayers to warn me that I’ve been marked. And when the choir sings certain lines, especially about sin or mercy or judgment, I feel it in my whole body. I know they are really warning me.

It’s like the message is hidden from everyone else, or maybe they just don’t understand it, but I do. I hear it and I know the church is suffering because I brought this on us. I know people want me to say maybe I’m just feeling guilty, but it doesn’t feel like maybe. It feels absolutely true to me.

doctor.question: Do you ever feel that your guilt or sins are so great that they can never be forgiven, or that you are uniquely marked by God in a way that others cannot understand or see?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep telling them I’m the reason my friend died, because I didn’t call her back and I had ugly thoughts sometimes, and I know the Lord is punishing everybody at church because of me.
target_item.reason: The question is most directly asking about overwhelming, possibly delusional guilt and beliefs about being unforgivable or punished because of sins.

patient.answer:
Yes… I do feel that. I feel like what I did can’t really be forgiven, not in the way people at church talk about forgiveness. They say the Lord forgives if you repent, and I’ve tried to repent, I have, over and over, but it doesn’t feel like it reaches Him. It feels like my prayers just stop somewhere because what I did was too bad.

I keep going back to my friend. I keep telling them—I keep telling everybody who will listen—that I’m the reason she died. If I had called her back when I should have, if I hadn’t been selfish or tired or irritated or whatever was wrong with me that day… maybe she would still be here. And it’s not only the phone call. It’s what was in my heart. I had ugly thoughts sometimes. Thoughts I shouldn’t have had. Mean, impatient thoughts. And I think the Lord saw all of that, not just what I did but what kind of person I really am inside.

And yes, I feel marked. I don’t think other people can see it the way I do, and they tell me I’m wrong, but I feel like God knows. I feel like He has singled me out because I brought this punishment on everybody at church. Those people don’t deserve to suffer because of me, but I know the Lord is punishing them because of what I did. That’s what makes it worse. If it were only me, maybe I could bear it, but I think I’ve brought it onto them too.

Yes… yes, I do believe that. I know other people don’t hear it the way I do, and I know if you were sitting beside me you might say it’s just a prayer or just a hymn, but it isn’t just that to me.

When the pastor is praying, certain words stand out like they’re being sent straight through him to me. It feels like God is warning me, like He has marked me because of what I’ve done. And when the choir sings certain lines—about sin, mercy, judgment, suffering—I can’t just hear them as songs anymore. I hear them as a message. A warning.

And I know others don’t seem to notice. They just sit there, they sing along, they bow their heads, they act like church is normal. But I feel it so strongly that the church is suffering because I brought this on us. Like the punishment is there, but only I understand why it’s happening. It’s because of me.
